name: Johan H. Andresen
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Ferd AS (Oslo)
profile: Fifth-generation head of the Andresen family business (Tiedemanns tobacco, bought 1849), which he renamed Ferd in 2001 and turned into a Nordic investment group (Elopak, Aibel, Swix, real estate, funds). CEO 1998-2012, chairman since 2012; in 2007 he passed most shares to daughters Katharina and Alexandra, and in Dec 2023 said his A-shares will go to a Ferd Foundation.
interesting_fact: In 2006 he bid about NOK 11 billion for Swiss packaging maker SIG to merge it with Elopak, which would have made the world's No. 2 packaging group; he dropped the bid in 2007 after a bidding war.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family business he worked as a product manager at International Paper in the US (1989-91). In 2009 he founded Ferd Social Entrepreneurs, and he helped launch the Norwegian Microfinance Initiative (2008). He has also chaired the Council on Ethics for Norway's Government Pension Fund Global.
notes: Dropped the 'Jr.' from his name after his father died in 2011. Ferd's 2023 annual report lists Ferd JHA AS (100% his) as a shareholder alongside his daughters' holding companies. For an energy angle, Ferd co-owns the oil-services firm Aibel.

name: Nirmal Kumar Minda
current_role: Chairman (Executive Chairman), UNO Minda Ltd; President of ASSOCHAM for 2025
profile: Second-generation head of UNO Minda (formerly Minda Industries), a Gurugram-based maker of auto switches, lighting, alloy wheels and EV components. He joined his father Shadilal's business in 1977 and ran it on his own after a 1996 split with his brother. He built it through Japanese and European joint ventures and moved from MD to Chairman in April 2025.
interesting_fact: The business goes back to 1958, when his father Shadilal Minda started importing ammeters from Japan. It moved to Delhi in 1962 to serve the tractor and motorcycle aftermarket.
deep_cut_fact: The group's first joint venture (1995) came from a quality push by Maruti. Minda asked the carmaker to help find a Japanese partner for switches, which led to Toyota-group supplier Tokai Rika. Separately, he and his wife Suman run Samarth-Jyoti, which operates two schools, a 100-bed hospital and 18 village centres.
notes: The Samarth-Jyoti detail comes from an India CSR profile (https://indiacsr.in/biography-nirmal-kumar-minda-president-assocham-2025/). EV components and ASSOCHAM policy work are possible podcast angles. Sources differ on his exact title (Chairman vs Chairman & MD).

name: Edward J. DeBartolo, Jr.
current_role: Founder and CEO, DeBartolo Holdings LLC (Tampa, FL)
profile: Son of mall pioneer Edward J. DeBartolo Sr. He joined the family's Edward J. DeBartolo Corp. in 1971 and led its 1996 merger with Simon Property Group. He owned the San Francisco 49ers from 1977 to 2000, a stretch that brought five Super Bowl titles. Since 2002 he has run DeBartolo Holdings, which covers real estate development, private equity investments, sports and philanthropy.
interesting_fact: Inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2016 as a contributor. Steve Young credited his 'family approach', which treated players as partners, with changing how NFL owners run teams.
deep_cut_fact: In 2007 he co-founded Brooks-DeBartolo Collegiate High School in Tampa with Hall of Fame linebacker Derrick Brooks. At the 2014 flag-football game that was Candlestick Park's last football event, Joe Montana threw him the final touchdown pass.
notes: No published email. DeBartolo Holdings lists a main office line, 813.908.8400, at its Tampa HQ (debartoloholdings.com contact section). Avoid his 1998 Edwin Edwards case and the 2020 pardon. Debartolo.com is a parked domain, not his.

name: Jonathan Nelson
current_role: Founder and Executive Chairman, Providence Equity Partners
profile: Jonathan M. Nelson (Brown '77) co-founded Providence Equity Partners in Providence, RI in 1989. It has since backed more than 180 media, communications, education and information companies. Wins include selling PADI in 2017 for over $700M and roughly sextupling a $300M 2007 stake in ZeniMax when Microsoft bought it for $7.5B. He is now executive chairman and a trustee of Rockefeller University.
interesting_fact: In college he worked at a commercial radio station, hosting the 'Jazz After Hours' program. Today he sits on the board of the Newport Festival Foundation, which runs the Newport Folk and Jazz Festivals.
deep_cut_fact: In 2016 his $25 million gift created the Jonathan M. Nelson Center for Entrepreneurship at his alma mater, Brown. He had earlier funded Brown's Nelson Fitness Center, and he serves as a Fellow of the Brown Corporation.

public_contacts.value: Pro-Providence@profileadvisors.com (Profile Advisors, listed as Providence Equity media contact)

notes: Media enquiries go through the PR firm Profile Advisors. The Brown entrepreneurship center and his jazz/Newport interests make good outreach hooks. Providence invests in communications infrastructure, which is relevant to data centers.
